claim: Bacteriophage PR772 is a member of the Tectiviridae family.
source: Bacteriophage PR772, a member of the Tectiviridae family, has a 70 nm diameter icosahedral protein capsid that encapsulates a lipid membrane, dsDNA, and various internal proteins.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: Bacteriophage PR772 has a 70 nm diameter icosahedral protein capsid.
source: Bacteriophage PR772, a member of the Tectiviridae family, has a 70 nm diameter icosahedral protein capsid that encapsulates a lipid membrane, dsDNA, and various internal proteins.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract and supported by structural data.

claim: The overall resolution of the PR772 virion is 2.75 Å.
source: The overall resolution of the virion is 2.75 Å, while the resolution of the protein capsid is 2.3 Å.
evidence: Resolution determined by Fourier shell correlation (FSC) @0.143 as stated in the Results section.

claim: The resolution of the protein capsid is 2.3 Å.
source: The overall resolution of the virion is 2.75 Å, while the resolution of the protein capsid is 2.3 Å.
evidence: Resolution determined by local resolution estimation using ResMap.

claim: The conventional penta-symmetron formed by the capsomeres is replaced by a large vertex complex in the pseudo T = 25 capsid.
source: The conventional penta-symmetron formed by the capsomeres is replaced by a large vertex complex in the pseudo T = 25 capsid.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural analysis.

claim: All the vertices contain the host-recognition protein, P5.
source: All the vertices contain the host-recognition protein, P5; two of these vertices show the presence of the receptor-binding protein, P2.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by localized reconstruction data.

claim: Two of the vertices show the presence of the receptor-binding protein, P2.
source: All the vertices contain the host-recognition protein, P5; two of these vertices show the presence of the receptor-binding protein, P2.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by 3D classification showing P2 in 16% of sub-particles.

claim: The 3D structure of the vertex complex shows interactions with the viral membrane.
source: The 3D structure of the vertex complex shows interactions with the viral membrane, indicating a possible mechanism for viral infection.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural data showing P16 interactions.

claim: Bacteriophage PR772 is a double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) virus.
source: Bacteriophage PR772 is a ﻿double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) virus with a 70 nm diameter icosahedral protein capsid encapsulating the internal lipid bilayer along with numerous proteins and a 15 kbp long linear genome.
evidence: Stated directly in the Introduction.

claim: PR772 has a 15 kbp long linear genome.
source: Bacteriophage PR772 is a ﻿double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) virus with a 70 nm diameter icosahedral protein capsid encapsulating the internal lipid bilayer along with numerous proteins and a 15 kbp long linear genome.
evidence: Stated directly in the Introduction.

claim: PR772 belongs to the Tectiviridae family and infects gram negative hosts like Escherichia coli, ﻿Salmonella typhimurium and other bacteria.
source: It belongs to the Tectiviridae family and infects gram negative hosts like Escherichia coli, ﻿Salmonella typhimurium and other bacteria, carrying a R772 plasmid-encoded receptor complex through which DNA can be transported during bacterial conjugation (Coetzee et al., 1979; Coetzee and Bekker, 1979; Mäntynen et al., 2019; Reddy et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: PR772 infects bacteria carrying a R772 plasmid-encoded receptor complex through which DNA can be transported during bacterial conjugation.
source: It belongs to the Tectiviridae family and infects gram negative hosts like Escherichia coli, ﻿Salmonella typhimurium and other bacteria, carrying a R772 plasmid-encoded receptor complex through which DNA can be transported during bacterial conjugation (Coetzee et al., 1979; Coetzee and Bekker, 1979; Mäntynen et al., 2019; Reddy et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Much of the functional knowledge of the viral proteins is inferred from previous studies on PRD1, a close relative of PR772 with a genome sequence identity of 97.2%.
source: Much of the functional knowledge of the viral proteins is inferred from previous studies on PRD1, a close relative of PR772 with a genome sequence identity of 97.2% (Lute et al., 2004; Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Members of the Tectiviridae family that infect Gram-negative bacteria have an inner lipid membrane and lack a tail in the dormant viral particle.
source: The most striking features of phages from those members of the Tectiviridae family that infect Gram-negative bacteria, is the presence of an inner lipid membrane and lack of a tail in the dormant viral particle.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction.

claim: During infection, Tectiviridae viruses produce a membranous tube derived from the inner membrane of the viral particle, lined from the inside by proteins P7, P11 and P32.
source: During the process of infection, these viruses produce a membranous tube derived from the inner membrane of the viral particle, lined from the inside by proteins P7, P11 and P32. This tube is used to inject the viral dsDNA into the host (Peralta et al., 2013; Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The membranous tube is used to inject the viral dsDNA into the host.
source: During the process of infection, these viruses produce a membranous tube derived from the inner membrane of the viral particle, lined from the inside by proteins P7, P11 and P32. This tube is used to inject the viral dsDNA into the host (Peralta et al., 2013; Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Genome analysis of PR772 identified 32 open reading frames (ORFs) containing at least 40 codons.
source: Genome analysis of PR772 identified 32 open reading frames (ORFs) containing at least 40 codons (Lute et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Twenty-eight annotated proteins are known to be expressed from the PR772 genome, of which three do not make it into the final assembly.
source: Twenty-eight annotated proteins are known to be expressed from the genome, of which three do not make it into the final assembly (Butcher et al., 2012; Lute et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In PRD1, the capsid is formed by proteins P3 (major capsid protein), P30 (capsid associated protein) and the vertex complex.
source: In previous studies on PRD1, it was shown that the capsid is formed by proteins P3 (major capsid protein), P30 (capsid associated protein) and the vertex complex.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction based on previous studies.

claim: The vertex complex includes the penton protein (P31), the host-recognition protein (P5) and the receptor-binding protein (P2) along with the infectivity protein (P16).
source: The vertex complex includes the penton protein (P31), the host-recognition protein (P5) and the receptor-binding protein (P2) along with the infectivity protein (P16) that acts as a cementing protein, holding the vertex complex together and also stabilizing the pseudo-icosahedral capsid of the virus (Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: P16 acts as a cementing protein, holding the vertex complex together and also stabilizing the pseudo-icosahedral capsid of the virus.
source: The vertex complex includes the penton protein (P31), the host-recognition protein (P5) and the receptor-binding protein (P2) along with the infectivity protein (P16) that acts as a cementing protein, holding the vertex complex together and also stabilizing the pseudo-icosahedral capsid of the virus (Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Proteins P6, P9, P20 and P22 are involved in DNA packaging.
source: Proteins P6, P9, P20 and P22 are involved in DNA packaging and proteins P7, P14, P11, P18, P32 and P34 are responsible for DNA delivery to the host (Grahn et al., 2002; Lute et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Proteins P7, P14, P11, P18, P32 and P34 are responsible for DNA delivery to the host.
source: Proteins P6, P9, P20 and P22 are involved in DNA packaging and proteins P7, P14, P11, P18, P32 and P34 are responsible for DNA delivery to the host (Grahn et al., 2002; Lute et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The Tectiviridae family of viruses have structural similarities to adenovirus.
source: The Tectiviridae family of viruses are also known to have structural similarities to adenovirus (Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: In-vitro protein expression studies showed that P31 forms pentamers and P5 form multimers of trimers.
source: The in-vitro protein expression studies showed that P31 forms pentamers and P5 form multimers of trimers (i.e, (P53)1, (P53)2, (P53)3) (Sokolova et al., 2001).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: P31- mutants produced incomplete PRD1 particles that lacked P31, P5 and P2 functions and failed to form the vertex complex.
source: The gene knock-out studies showed that P31- mutants produced incomplete PRD1 particles that lacked P31, P5 and P2 functions. They failed to form the vertex complex.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction based on gene knock-out studies.

claim: A P5- mutant produced intact viral particle but lacked both P5 and P2 functions.
source: A P5- mutant produced intact viral particle but lacked both P5 and P2 functions (Rydman et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The high resolution x-ray crystallographic structure of the P2 protein is known.
source: The high resolution x-ray crystallographic structure of the P2 protein is known but the location and orientation with respect to the penton base in its functional form is currently not known (Xu et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The N-terminal region of the P3 subunits have three conformations, not two as previously described.
source: The high-resolution structure of PR772 confirms the previously shown variability of the N and C-terminals of the P3 protein depending on the locations within the trisymmetron. The high-resolution also allows us to extend the analysis of these conformations and show that the N-terminal of P3 can adopt three different conformations, not two as previously described. (Abrescia et al., 2004; Butcher et al., 2012) (Figures 2A and 3B).
evidence: Stated in the Introduction and supported by structural data in Results.

claim: The new N-terminal P3 conformation plays an important role in accommodating the P30 protein during particle assembly.
source: The new N-terminal P3 conformation plays an important role in accommodating the P30 protein during particle assembly.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction and supported by structural analysis.

claim: The C-terminal region of P3 helps in locking the adjacent trisymmetrons through a hinge mechanism.
source: The C-terminal region of P3 not only shows the formation of a β-sheet with P30 but also helps in locking the adjacent trisymmetrons through a hinge mechanism, thus facilitating the formation of icosahedral particles and regulating their size.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction and supported by structural data.

claim: Localized asymmetric reconstruction of the vertex region of PR772 revealed a P5-P31 heteropentameric base.
source: Localized asymmetric reconstruction of the vertex region of PR772 revealed a P5-P31 heteropentameric base and the binding of P2 to P5 in the complex.
evidence: Stated in the Introduction and supported by localized reconstruction data.

claim: The penton base is a heteropentamer consisting of three copies of P5 and two copies of P31.
source: Our studies show that unlike what was predicted for PRD1, the penton base of PR772 is an asymmetric heteropentamer consisting of three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion and supported by structural data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The local resolution estimated using ResMap showed that most of the capsid was resolved to 2.3 Å.
source: The local resolution estimated using the two unfiltered final half maps with ResMap (Kucukelbir et al., 2014) showed that most of the capsid was resolved to 2.3 Å (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The resolution of the regions that interact with the inner lipid bilayer was lower at about 3.2 Å.
source: The resolution of the regions that interact with the inner lipid bilayer was lower at about 3.2 Å (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The areas around the icosahedral five-fold axes had resolutions varying between 2.3–3.0 Å.
source: The areas around the icosahedral five-fold axes had resolutions varying between 2.3–3.0 Å (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: At a root mean square deviation (RMSD) of 4.2, the side chains of the amino acid residues were visible for most of the capsid region.
source: At a root mean square deviation (RMSD; deviation away from noise as visualized in Coot, where noise is 0) of 4.2, the side chains of the amino acid residues were visible for most of the capsid region.
evidence: Stated in Results based on map quality assessment.

claim: The inner membrane layers of lipid, protein and dsDNA were smeared due to averaging and symmetry mismatch.
source: The inner membrane layers of lipid, protein and dsDNA were smeared due to averaging and symmetry mismatch.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: PR772 follows a pseudo T = 25 lattice architecture with a (h,k) of (0,5) resulting in an icosahedral structure with 20 large trisymmetrons and 12 penta-symmetrons.
source: The CryoEM 3D reconstruction of PR772 shows that the viral particle follows a pseudo T = 25 lattice architecture with a (h,k) of (0,5) resulting in an icosahedral structure with 20 large trisymmetrons and 12 penta-symmetrons (Caspar and Klug, 1962; Wrigley, 1969).
evidence: Stated in Results with supporting citations.

claim: Each trisymmetron has 36 copies of P3, the major capsid protein (MCP), arranged as 12 trimers.
source: Each of these trisymmetrons have 36 copies of P3, the major capsid protein (MCP), arranged as 12 trimers, each of which structurally appears to be hexagonal in shape.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: At the fivefold vertices, typical penta-symmetrons are replaced by vertex complexes to complete the icosahedral shell.
source: At the fivefold vertices, typical penta-symmetrons are replaced by vertex complexes to complete the icosahedral shell.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: PR772 is one of the larger wild type viruses resolved to a resolution below 3 Å.
source: With a pseudo T = 25 architecture, PR772 is one of the larger wild type viruses resolved to a resolution below 3 Å.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural data.

claim: P3 monomers exhibit the double-barrel trimer arrangement, as previously seen in viruses of the adenovirus linage.
source: They exhibit the double-barrel trimer arrangement, as previously seen in viruses of the adenovirus linage (Benson et al., 1999; Reddy et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated in Results with supporting citations.

claim: The Leu130 - Ala150 loops from subunits a, b and c of P3 interact with each other in a cyclic manner at the centre of the trimer complex to stabilize it.
source: The Leu130 - Ala150 loops from subunits a, b and c of P3 interact with each other in a cyclic manner at the centre of the trimer complex to stabilize it (Figure 2).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The N-terminal of the P3 monomers have three different conformations: a helix turn helix, a long helix and a long helix with a kink.
source: The N-terminal of the P3 monomers have three different conformations; a helix turn helix, a long helix and a long helix with a kink (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: When the N-terminal adopts a helix turn helix, the shorter helix close to the N-terminal is bent away from the lipid membrane and interacts with the adjacent subunit of the trimer.
source: When the N-terminal adopts a helix turn helix, the shorter helix close to the N-terminal is bent away from the lipid membrane and interacts with the adjacent subunit of the trimer.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: In case of the long helical conformation, the N-terminal residues Met1 – Gln6 anchor the P3 subunit to the lipid membrane.
source: In case of the long helical conformation, the N-terminal residues Met1 – Gln6 anchor the P3 subunit to the lipid membrane (Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The N-terminal region of subunit a is more flexible as compared to the same region of subunits b or c in the four unique trimers.
source: The N-terminal region of subunit a is more flexible as compared to the same region of subunits b or c in the four unique trimers.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: The N-terminal of the b subunits always forms a long helix that anchors the subunit to the membrane.
source: The N-terminal of the b subunits always forms a long helix that anchors the subunit to the membrane (Figure 2C–F and Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figures 2C-F and 3A.

claim: The C-termini of P3 trimers adopt four different conformations.
source: The C-termini are more variable as compared to the N-termini of the trimers. They adopt four different conformations; one conformation is a long strand extending towards the lipid membrane and found in subunit b of all trimers (Figure 2C–F,H–K).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: P5 residues Trp121 - Gly124 extend upwards filling the map density, but there is no contribution from P31.
source: P31 terminates close to the fivefold and thus cannot form the stem-like protrusion whereas P5 residues (121-124) continue up and outward and these residues have the potential to form the stem-like protrusion (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 form the penton base in PR772.
source: By this it can be concluded that 3 copies of P5 and 2 copies of P31 form the penton base in PR772 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The stalk-like density observed, emanating from the penton base, is built with three copies of the P5 protein, forming a collagen-like motif.
source: With the localized asymmetric reconstruction and focused classification methods, the structure and composition of the penton base was established. It is now known that the stalk-like density observed, emanating from the penton base, is built with three copies of the P5 protein, forming a collagen-like motif and eventually the unresolved knob domain.
evidence: Stated in Results based on localized reconstruction.

claim: The crystal structure of P2 (PDB:1N7U) from PRD1 has 98% protein sequence identity to PR772.
source: The crystal structure of P2 (PDB:1N7U) from PRD1 (98% protein sequence identity to PR772) was fitted into the density.
evidence: Stated in Results.

claim: The interaction of P5 with P2 can be compared to a ball and socket joint.
source: The interaction of P5 with P2 can be compared to a ball and socket joint, for instance as seen in a human shoulder, where the N-terminal base of P5 is the ball with domain I and domain II of P2 acting as a socket (Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: Stated in Results and illustrated in Figure 5—video 1.

claim: The estimation of the electrostatic surface potential of both P2 and P5 shows good charge complementarity in and around the regions of interaction.
source: The estimation of the electrostatic surface potential of both P2 and P5 shows good charge complementarity in and around the regions of interaction. These regions also have similar hydrophobicity (Kyte-Doolittle scale) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: P2 interacts with the collagen-like motif of the P5 stalk, thus introducing some rigidity to the C-terminal of the P5 trimer.
source: P2 also interacts with the collagen-like motif of the P5 stalk, thus introducing some rigidity to the C-terminal of the P5 trimer.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: The presence of P2 nudges the P5 stalk by ~36° from its usual position.
source: The presence of P2 nudges the P5 stalk by ~36O from its usual position (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: The P5 stalk acts as a linchpin that locks the P2 molecule and restricts it from swivelling around the 5-fold vertex.
source: The P5 stalk acts as a linchpin that locks the P2 molecule and restricts it from swivelling around the 5-fold vertex, thus stabilizing the complex.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: The occupancy of P2 on the 5-fold vertices appears to be significantly lower in bacteriophage PR772 than what was observed from other members of the Tectiviridae family.
source: The occupancy of P2 on the 5-fold vertices appears to be significantly lower in bacteriophage PR772 than what was observed from other members of the Tectiviridae family.
evidence: Stated in Results based on 3D classification data.

claim: Only 467,631 sub-particles from a total of 3,340,224 extracted sub-particles showed the presence of a density representing P2, accounting for 16% of all the sub-particles used or about two vertices in an intact viral particle.
source: The 3D classification of the signal subtracted and isolated vertices revealed that only 467,631 sub-particles from a total of 3,340,224 extracted sub-particles, showed the presence of a density representing P2. This accounts for 16% of all the sub-particles used or about two vertices in an intact viral particle, assuming an equal distribution among the viral particles.
evidence: Stated in Results based on 3D classification data.

claim: P30 adopts an extended conformation in an intact viral particle and it is found wedged in between the trisymmetrons.
source: P30 adopts an extended conformation in an intact viral particle and it is found wedged in between the trisymmetrons (Figure 2A, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Two copies of P30, interlocked at the N-terminal hook, span between the adjacent vertices.
source: Two copies of P30, interlocked at the N-terminal hook, span between the adjacent vertices.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: In an intact viral particle, P30 forms a cage-like structure, which stabilizes the trisymmetrons themselves and also interact with the neighboring trisymmetrons to form a closed network.
source: In an intact viral particle, P30 forms a cage-like structure, which stabilizes the trisymmetrons themselves and also interact with the neighboring trisymmetrons to form a closed network (Figure 2A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The residues Tyr62 – Ile64 and Val32 – Arg35 of P30 form beta sheets with residues Thr384 – Leu386 from subunit c of P3 trimer one and residues Thr384 – Asn388 from subunit c of P3 trimer two respectively.
source: The residues Tyr62 – Ile64 and Val32 – Arg35 of P30 form beta sheets with residues Thr384 – Leu386 from subunit c of P3 trimer one and residues Thr384 – Asn388 from subunit c of P3 trimer two respectively (Figure 2A highlighted regions).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Five copies of P16 bridge the penton to the five trisymmetrons that meet at the vertex complex.
source: Five copies of P16 bridge the penton to the five trisymmetrons that meet at the vertex complex.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: The long C-terminal trans-membrane helix of P16 (Leu7 - Ala28) was poorly resolved and barely visible at 0.6 RMSD.
source: The long C-terminal trans-membrane helix of P16 (Leu7 - Ala28) was poorly resolved and barely visible at 0.6 RMSD.
evidence: Stated in Results based on map quality assessment.

claim: P16 forms a clamp-like complex using the loop Asn44 -Val55 and helix Asn101 - Ala115, which attaches onto the loop Val242 - Tyr247 of one of the P3 subunits of trimer one and locks it with the adjacent P3 subunit of trimer one from the neighboring trisymmetrons.
source: However, the partial model shows that P16 forms a clamp-like complex using the loop Asn44 -Val55 and helix Asn101 - Ala115, which attaches onto the loop Val242 - Tyr247 of one of the P3 subunits of trimer one and locks it with the adjacent P3 subunit of trimer one from the neighboring trisymmetrons (Figure 6B).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In case of P5, the C-terminal Gly84 of P30 seems to interact with the Met19 residue of a P5 subunit by a hydrophobic interaction.
source: In case of P5, the C-terminal Gly84 of P30 seems to interact with the Met19 residue of a P5 subunit by a hydrophobic interaction (Figure 6A).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 are held together by their N-terminal residues.
source: Three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 are held together by their N-terminal residues.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: Met9 – Val14 of P31 and Ser9 – Tyr13 of P5 inter-digit with the neighboring subunit of the pentamer as β-sheets.
source: Met9 – Val14 of P31 and Ser9 – Tyr13 of P5 inter-digit with the neighboring subunit of the pentamer as β-sheets.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: Residues Gln8 – Asn2 and Gly8 – Met1 of P31 and P5 respectively continue further and hug the neighboring subunits.
source: Residues Gln8 – Asn2 and Gly8 – Met1 of P31 and P5 respectively continue further and hug the neighboring subunits (Figure 4—figure supplement 7).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 7.

claim: There is no obvious direct interaction between the penton and the P3 subunits of the capsid except for the special cases where N-terminal residues of P5 are wedged in between the adjacent P3 subunits.
source: There is no obvious direct interaction between the penton and the P3 subunits of the capsid except for the special cases mentioned above.
evidence: Stated in Results based on structural analysis.

claim: The disorganised region of P16 seems to interact with the penton base and helps in binding the vertex complex to the trisymmetrons.
source: The disorganised region of P16 seems to interact with the penton base and helps in binding the vertex complex to the trisymmetrons (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Stated in Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Each trisymmetron of PR772 is composed of 12 trimers of the P3 protein that are in turn bound by P30, an overall arrangement similar to that of the close relative PRD1.
source: Each trisymmetron of PR772 is composed of 12 trimers of the P3 protein that are in turn bound by P30, an overall arrangement similar to that of the close relative PRD1 (Abrescia et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: The newly discovered conformation of the N-terminal region of P3, a long helix with a kink, is structurally critical to accommodate the interlocking region formed by the N-terminal hooks of P30 during the initiation of particle assembly.
source: The newly discovered conformation of the N-terminal region of P3, a long helix with a kink, is structurally critical to accommodate the interlocking region formed by the N-terminal hooks of P30 during the initiation of particle assembly.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: The N-terminal region of P3 shows plasticity and play an important role in both stabilizing the trimer and anchoring the trimer complex to the membrane.
source: The N-terminal region of P3 shows plasticity and play an important role in both stabilizing the trimer and anchoring the trimer complex to the membrane.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: The presence of P16 close to the penton region makes the interaction of all the neighboring trimer one more stable and also anchors the whole vertex complex to the membrane.
source: The presence of P16 close to the penton region makes the interaction of all the neighboring trimer one more stable (Figure 6) and also anchors the whole vertex complex to the membrane (Figure 7), emphasizing the role of P30 and P16 in maintaining the size and structure of the icosahedral viral capsid.
evidence: Stated in Discussion and shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: P31 would promote the formation of an intact viral particle by avoiding the steric-hinderances that could occur during the formation of the vertex complex, if the P31 subunits were replaced by P5.
source: With the current model, P31 would promote the formation of an intact viral particle by avoiding the steric-hinderances that could occur during the formation of the vertex complex, if the P31 subunits were replaced by P5.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: A penton with 3 copies of the P5 subunits will support the formation of a stable collagen-like motif and the formation of the C-terminal host recognition domain of P5.
source: A penton with 3 copies of the P5 subunits will support (i) the formation of a stable collagen-like motif (Figure 7) and (ii) the formation of the C-terminal host recognition domain of P5.
evidence: Stated in Discussion and shown in Figure 7.

claim: A heteropentameric base of the vertex complex with three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 address both the issues of forming a stable collagen-like motif and the C-terminal host recognition domain of P5.
source: A heteropentameric base of the vertex complex with three copies of P5 and two copies of P31 address both these issues.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: The members of the Tectiviridae family have been shown to have structural similarities with adenoviruses despite infecting different hosts.
source: The members of the Tectiviridae family have been shown to have structural similarities with adenoviruses despite infecting different hosts.
evidence: Stated in Discussion.

claim: In adenoviruses, the symmetry mismatch seen in the vertex region is solved by the interaction of the tail region of the trimeric fibre with three of the five grooves formed by the subunits of the penton base.
source: In adenoviruses, the symmetry mismatch seen in the vertex region is solved by the interaction of the tail region of the trimeric fibre with three of the five grooves formed by the subunits of the penton base (Cao et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: In PR772, the symmetry mismatch problem is solved by domain swapping where the trimeric P5 protein swaps the N-terminal base domain with three copies of the P31 protein.
source: Unlike in adenoviruses, a similar problem in PR772 is solved by domain swapping. The trimeric P5 protein responsible for the formation of the spike, swaps the N-terminal base domain with three copies of the P31 protein (Figure 4F).
evidence: Stated in Discussion and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In the current CryoEM data, the orientation of P2 with respect to the penton base is reversed when compared to what was described for PRD1.
source: In the current CryoEM data, the orientation of P2 with respect to the penton base is reversed when compared to what was described for PRD1 (Huiskonen et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The beta-propeller motif of P2 with domain I and II, interacts with the N-terminal base of P5 and also with the stalk.
source: Here, the beta-propeller motif of P2 with domain I and II, interacts with the N-terminal base of P5 and also with the stalk.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: Members of the Tectiviridae family with large sequence variation in the beta-propeller motif of P2 also showed variations in the P5 subunit as a compensatory effect.
source: This was also speculated on in a previous study, where it was noted that members of the Tectiviridae family with large sequence variation in the beta-propeller motif of P2 also showed variations in the P5 subunit as a compensatory effect (Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: P2 interacts with both the N-terminal base and the stalk region of P5 but does not interact directly with any other structural protein in PR772.
source: P2 interacts with both the N-terminal base and the stalk region of P5 but does not interact directly with any other structural protein in PR772.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: In the case of PRD1, P2 seems to occupy all vertices except for the unique packaging vertex.
source: In the case of PRD1, P2 seems to occupy all vertices except for the unique packaging vertex (Butcher et al., 2012; Caldentey et al., 2000; Saren et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: In PRD1, the loss of P2 from a packed viral particle resulted in spontaneous release of genomic DNA, leading to loss of infectivity and the formation of empty particles.
source: In PRD1, it was shown that the loss of P2 from a packed viral particle, resulted in spontaneous release of genomic DNA, leading to loss of infectivity and the formation of empty particles (Grahn et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: In a previous study of PR772, after purification, the concentration estimates of the particle by plaque assay and nano-particle tracking analysis were similar.
source: In a previous study of PR772, it was shown that after purification, the concentration estimates of the particle by plaque assay and nano-particle tracking analysis were similar (Reddy et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: PR772 particles remained intact and infectious after purification.
source: PR772 particles remained intact and infectious after purification.
evidence: Stated in Discussion.

claim: The presence of P2 in the vertex complex may coincide with the N-terminal region of P5 adopting the special conformation.
source: The presence of P2 in the vertex complex may coincide with the N-terminal region of P5 adopting the special conformation.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: The CryoEM map of sus690, a mutant PRD1 virion that lacks P2 and P5, showed absence of density in the region where the N-terminal of P5 is wedged between two neighboring P3 subunits.
source: It was reported that, compared to the CryoEM map of a wild type PRD1 virion, the CryoEM map of sus690, a mutant PRD1 virion that lacks P2 and P5, showed absence of density in the region where we see the N-terminal of P5 wedged between two neighboring P3 subunits.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on comparison with previous studies.

claim: In PR772, the copy number of P14, the occurrence of the special conformation of the N-terminal region of P5 protein and the number of P2 proteins packed in an intact viral particle seems to be related.
source: In PR772, the copy number of P14, the occurrence of the special conformation of the N-terminal region of P5 protein and the number of P2 proteins packed in an intact viral particle seems to be related.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis and comparison with PRD1.

claim: In PR772, the presence of the larger P7 protein in higher numbers at the vertex might hinder the formation of the special conformation of the N-terminal region of P5, which could reduce the number of P2 proteins packed in the particle.
source: In PR772, the presence of the larger P7 protein in higher numbers at the vertex (along with other proteins in the disordered region) might hinder the formation of the special conformation of the N-terminal region of P5, which could reduce the number of P2 proteins packed in the particle.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis and comparison with PRD1.

claim: The difference density map of the vertex region and the modeled penton shows that the disordered region of P16 interacts with the penton.
source: The difference density map of the vertex region and the modeled penton shows that the disordered region of P16 interacts with the penton (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Stated in Discussion and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The interactions of P16 with P3, P5, P31 along with the membrane seem to play a central role in the formation of the vertex complex and anchoring it to the membrane.
source: These interactions of P16 with P3, P5, P31 along with the membrane seem to play a central role in the formation of the vertex complex and anchoring it to the membrane.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: In earlier Raman spectroscopy studies on PRD1, it was shown that in the initial stages of viral assembly, P3 and P5 formed a precursor shell assisted by assembly factors and other membrane-associated proteins such as P16.
source: In earlier Raman spectroscopy studies on PRD1, it was shown that in the initial stages of viral assembly, P3 and P5 formed a precursor shell assisted by assembly factors and other membrane-associated proteins such as P16 (Bamford et al., 1990; Bamford et al., 1995).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: In PR772, the P5 trimers could be accommodated during the formation of the procapsid and two copies of P31 are later added to the penton region, forming a heteropentameric penton.
source: Similarly, in PR772 the P5 trimers could be accommodated during the formation of the procapsid and two copies of P31 are later added to the penton region, forming a heteropentameric penton.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis and comparison with PRD1.

claim: The map density below the P5 subunits is significantly different when compared to the same region below the P31 subunits.
source: From the localized asymmetric reconstruction of the vertex complex, one can notice that there is a variation in the map density below the penton. The map density below the P5 subunits is significantly different when compared to the same region below the P31 subunits.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: Along with the interactions of P16 with P5 and P31, there could also be poorly resolved proteins like P11, P7, P14 or P18 in the region below the penton.
source: This suggests that, along with the interactions of P16 with P5 and P31, there could also be poorly resolved proteins like P11, P7, P14 or P18, etc; in the region (Luo et al., 1993; Mattila et al., 2015; Rydman and Bamford, 2000).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Preliminary results for the whole particle asymmetric reconstruction using symmetry relaxation in EMAN2 of the wild type PR772 do not show the presence of a unique packaging portal in the dormant particle in contrast to PRD1.
source: Preliminary results for the whole particle asymmetric reconstruction using symmetry relaxation in EMAN2 of the wild type PR772 do not show the presence of a unique packaging portal in the dormant particle in contrast to PRD1.
evidence: Stated in Discussion based on preliminary asymmetric reconstruction.

claim: All the vertices of PR772 show the heteropentameric arrangement of the penton with three subunits showing the stalk and the other two without the stalk.
source: All the vertices of PR772 show the heteropentameric arrangement of the penton with three subunits showing the stalk and the other two without the stalk (Figure 4C–D, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Stated in Discussion and shown in Figure 4C-D and Supplementary file 2.

claim: P5 is needed for host recognition, but the binding of P5 to the host is transient.
source: In analogy to studies on PRD1, it is known that P5 is needed for host recognition, but the binding of P5 to the host is transient (Grahn et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: The host binding is stabilized by the high-affinity interaction of P2 and its receptor, locking the viral particle to the host.
source: The host binding is stabilized by the high-affinity interaction of P2 and its receptor, locking the viral particle to the host (Grahn et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in Discussion with supporting citation.

claim: The relative changes between P5 and P2 upon binding to the receptor on the host could trigger the disruption of the vertex complex by pulling the N-terminal region of the P5 trimers that are wedged between the P3 subunits.
source: The relative changes between P5 and P2 upon binding to the receptor on the host could trigger the disruption of the vertex complex by pulling the N-terminal region of the P5 trimers that are wedged between the P3 subunits.
evidence: Stated in Discussion as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The disruption of the vertex complex will in turn disrupt the interaction between the P5 proteins and P30.
source: This will in turn disrupt the interaction between the P5 proteins and P30 as seen in Figure 6.
evidence: Stated in Discussion as part of the proposed mechanism and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The disruption cascades further and disturbs the interaction between P30 and P16, rendering the whole vertex complex unstable.
source: This disruption cascades further and disturbs the interaction between P30 and P16, rendering the whole vertex complex unstable.
evidence: Stated in Discussion as part of the proposed mechanism.

claim: P30 dimers could transduce the disruption effects to the neighboring vertices.
source: P30 dimers could also transduce these effects to the neighboring vertices.
evidence: Stated in Discussion as part of the proposed mechanism.

claim: The disruption of the vertex complex exposes the viral membrane and membranous proteins like P18, P11/P7, P32 etc; to the host surface to facilitate the formation of the membranous tube for DNA transport.
source: The disruption of the vertex complex exposes the viral membrane and membranous proteins like P18, P11/P7, P32 etc; to the host surface to facilitate the formation of the membranous tube for DNA transport.
evidence: Stated in Discussion as part of the proposed mechanism.

claim: P16, that holds the vertex complex, along with other membranous proteins, could act as a protein tether that would help in moving the lipid membrane closer to the host.
source: P16, that holds the vertex complex, along with other membranous proteins, could act as a protein tether that would help in moving the lipid membrane closer to the host (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in Discussion as part of the proposed mechanism and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Bacteriophage PR772 was propagated on Escherichia coli K12 J53-1.
source: Bacteriophage PR772 (ATCC BAA-769-B1) was propagated on Escherichia coli K12 J53-1.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The data were collected on a Titan KRIOS equipped with a K2 Summit direct electron detector and a GIF Quantum LS energy filter.
source: The data were collected on a Titan KRIOS (ThermoFisher) equipped with a K2 Summit (Gatan) direct electron detector and a GIF Quantum LS (Gatan) energy filter.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: All the data were collected at a magnification of 130 k in EFTEM mode with a pixel size of 1.06 Å.
source: All the data were collected at a magnification of 130 k in EFTEM mode with a pixel size of 1.06 Å.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The slit width of the energy filter was 20 eV.
source: The slit width of the energy filter was 20 eV.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The dose rate was 4.4 e- per Å2 per second with a total exposure of 9 s resulting in a total dose of ~40 e-/Å2.
source: The dose rate was 4.4 e- per Å2 per second with a total exposure of 9 s resulting in a total dose of ~40 e-/Å2.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The total dose was distributed over 40 frames in each movie.
source: The total dose was distributed over 40 frames in each movie.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: 3220 movies were collected.
source: 3220 movies were collected.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The movie frames were corrected for beam induced sample motion and aligned using MotionCor2.
source: The movie frames were corrected for beam induced sample motion and aligned using MotionCor2 (Zheng et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods with supporting citation.

claim: The first 3 frames of the movies were skipped and the rest were aligned.
source: The first 3 frames of the movies were skipped and the rest were aligned.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: The non-dose weighted image stacks were used to estimate defocus and correct CTF using CTFFIND4.
source: The non-dose weighted image stacks were used to estimate defocus and correct CTF using CTFFIND4 (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015).
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods with supporting citation.

claim: A total of ~3200 images were used to auto pick 56275 particles using template matching in RELION.
source: A total of ~3200 images were used to auto pick 56275 particles using template matching in RELION (Scheres, 2012) (version 2.1 beta 1) (Kimanius et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods with supporting citations.

claim: RELION: 3D initial model tool, which is based on stochastic gradient descent, was used to generate an ab-initio reference map for 3D classification.
source: RELION: 3D initial model tool, which is based on stochastic gradient descent, was used to generate an ab-initio reference map for 3D classification.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: After refinement, the maps were corrected for Ewald sphere effects using RELION 3.0 beta 2.
source: After refinement, the maps were corrected for Ewald sphere effects using RELION 3.0 beta 2.
evidence: Stated in Materials and methods.

claim: CryoEM Density maps and atomic models have been deposited in the Electron Microscopy Database and the Protein Databank with the accession codes EMD-4461, EMD-4462, EMD-10237, EMD-10238 and PDB ID 6Q5U.
source: ﻿CryoEM Density maps and atomic models that support the findings of this study have been deposited in the Electron Microscopy Database and the Protein Databank with the accession codes EMD-4461 (Whole particle reconstruction), EMD-4462 (Vertex Complex), EMD-10237 (Localized reconstruction of the penton region), EMD-10238 (Focused Classification of the penton region) and PDB ID 6Q5U (Atomic model of the asymmetric unit).
evidence: Stated in Data availability section.
